I have been reading applications for this program for nine years, which means I have read something like four thousand of them, and I can tell you the three things that make me stop. The first one is a number that is specific. Not many years of experience, but I have been doing this since 2016. The moment there is a date, I believe the rest of the paragraph. The second one is a detail from inside the work, the kind of thing you only know if you have been in the room. Somebody wrote to me last year that the hardest part of her job was not the music. It was telling a singer that the key was wrong on the day of the show. I have never forgotten that line. And the third thing is honesty about the gap. Everybody has a year that went quietly. The applications that hide it always look edited, and the ones that name it in six words never do.

Nobody has ever hired me because of my website. I have had one since 2014, I update it about once a year, and as far as I can tell it exists so that people who have already decided to hire me have somewhere to check that I am real. Every single job I have had has arrived the same way: somebody I worked with told somebody else. That is it. Word of mouth, since long before any of this was online. Which means the thing you are actually building is not a showreel. It is a memory in about forty people. And people remember two things about working with you, and neither of them is your best mix. They remember whether you were calm at eleven at night when something broke, and they remember whether you said the difficult thing early, while it could still be fixed. I have been doing this for fifteen years and I have never met an exception.
